channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Reluctant Wendigo" - A young man that can turn into a wendigo made of volcanic glass, whether he wants to or not.

item.title: Re: Reluctant Wendigo
item.content:encoded: Hmm, thats a good point. I suppose if you look into anything enough you'll find similarities. I suppose now that I think about it its a jekyll-hyde dynamic. There's the 'normal' side and the anomalous. I dont know, I feel this SCP deviates well enough. But as for Pharrow, I'll edit the idea above to indicate its merely an aspect of many, not the sole focus of the piece.

item.title: Re: Reluctant Wendigo
item.content:encoded:
1) Part of Doomsday's powerset is that any attack makes him add to his defenses in the form of bone spurs, much the same way your SCP grows obsidian. He's also a feral character, but where yours tend to flee and eat, Doomsday tends to attack and kill. Again, not saying to not pursue the idea based on that, especially as it looks like you're deviating far enough away from it.

[And yeah: SCP-682 is essentially the reptile version of Doomsday, but the symbology works out slightly different (more of a "we chained the monster" than "monster out to kill us".]

2) The "doctor becoming too familiar with his patient" is a standard trope, as is the "faithful worker finding problems with his object of worship". Again, not saying it's a bad thing, just be aware of the traps.

item.title: Re: Reluctant Wendigo
item.content:encoded: Ey, thanks for the reply. Isn't 682 just a reptile version of doomsday? That's rhetorical, dont answer that, but yeah, I suppose I can see where youre going with that. The issue is I'm afraid the 'idea' Ive put forward is vastly different to the actual draft in place. What is it that's similar to Doomsday? Just the adaptive 'super skin' type property? How would I pursue the parralels through a clinical, technical document other than an interview(which I plan to do)? Dr. Pharrow forming a friendship is more for the self-discovery of a man who's convinced himself there is no blurred line yet finds himself smudging it up. Perhaps it would find better traction if I cleared that up?

item.title: Re: Reluctant Wendigo
item.content:encoded:
1) NEVER, EVER express your own insignificance. Just don't do it.

2) The problem for me is that this sounds too much like an SCP version of Doomsday, from DC Comics. Also, there is the usual retread of questioning The Foundation's moral authority.

While I'm not saying you shouldn't pursue it based on that, I do think that pursuing it in parallel would be a more interesting way of approaching it: By looking at the asylum's process you could cast aspersion on The Foundation.

There's some fun you could have here, from a dramatic perspective, just try to avoid the usual cliches and it could work.

item.title: SCP-XXXX Reluctant Wendigo
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Folklore/Drama/a slight bit of humor.

Page Layout: Standard Description and Containment Procedures, interview, incident report, and requests. The SCP and its procedures are currently under review by the foundation ethics committee.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a young man that experiences anomalous growths over any injury he receives. If the injury is enough to incapacitate or "kill" the subject it will instead become enveloped in this obsidian-like substance[in the visage of a wendigo from Algonquin folklore] and attempt to consume the flesh of any organism it can. It must be noted that this material is impenetrable to known conventional means.

+ Central Narrative, Hook and Additional Notes
- collapse

Central Narrative: XXXX was discovered wandering along the highway after it was hit and incapacitated in a car crash on the I-15. Police reports indicate it terminated both the driver and all but one family member in the car before fleeing. Early interviews in containment suggest the entity gained its anomalous properties after being forced into a sanitarium for divergent behavior. This asylum practiced unsanctioned, immoral "treatments" on XXXX that would leave it with its anomalous properties. Basically, imagine "The Factory" but instead of churning out anomalous objects its anomalous humanoid entities.

While in containment the head researcher assigned for XXXX, Dr. Pharrow, interviews it for several psychological evaluations and learns of the existence of "Lindvell's Sanitorium for Ordinary Youth!" where each patient is somehow given anomalous properties to 'protect' or make 'useful' for potential adoptive parties. A later incident report indicates that an associate of Lindvell's Sanitorium facilitated a containment breach to retrieve XXXX for a "prospective and interested party." It is also within this report where it is discovered that XXXX can be knocked from its incapacitated state by sustained impacts from high velocity, high density projectiles.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A young man is forced to become an anomaly he has no control over. His body's defense mechanisms are hijacked, he cant die, only sent into a feral ravenous, starving state that spurs him to kill, to satiate.

Additional Notes: I…plan to pursue this sanitarium idea further in SCP Tales. I've most likely explained this poorly, and I apologize if so. Please do not hesitate to reply with questions or queries for clarification. Also if there is a similar SCP somewhere, please tell me, there are thousands of entries and I am incapable of trawling through every one.
